chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from 'Abbad ibn Sulayman from Sa'd ibn Sa'd from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed Dhuhr or 'Asr and then broke his ritual purity (hadath) when he sat in the fourth rak'ah. He said: 'If he had said the testimony of faith (shahadah), he does not need to repeat (the prayer); but if he had not yet said the testimony before breaking his purity, he should repeat (the prayer).'
ai.seo_question: Does a man need to repeat his prayer if he breaks ritual purity during the sitting in the fourth rak'ah?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the juristic distinction hinges on the recitation of the Tashahhud, which marks the completion of the prayer's essential pillars; thus, if the Shahadah was already recited, the minor impurity does not invalidate the completed act. This ruling reflects the Shia principle that the prayer is considered concluded once the final testimony is uttered, distinguishing it from schools of thought that may require the prayer to be repeated if impurity occurs before the final Salam. It underscores the importance of precise timing in ritual purity within the framework of Salah.
